problem.text: Kate bakes a $20$-inch by $18$-inch pan of cornbread. The cornbread is cut into pieces that measure $2$ inches by $2$ inches. How many pieces of cornbread does the pan contain?

steps.title: Where to start: count the pieces along each side
steps.body: The pieces are little squares laid out in rows and columns, like a grid. So count how many pieces fit along each side of the pan. Both $20$ and $18$ are even, so the $2$-inch pieces fit exactly with nothing left over.

your_turn.prompt: How many $2$-inch pieces fit along the $20$-inch side?

steps.title: A piece is not 2 square inches
steps.body: Another way to count is to divide the pan's area by the area of one piece. Careful: the pan's area is the number of square inches, not the number of pieces. And each piece is $2$ inches by $2$ inches, so you must divide by its area, not by $2$.

your_turn.prompt: What is the area of one piece of cornbread?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Along the $18$-inch side, $18 \div 2 = 9$ pieces fit. So the pan holds $10$ columns of $9$ pieces.
$$10 \times 9 = 90$$
Check by area: the pan is $20 \times 18 = 360$ square inches, and $360 \div 4 = 90$. The answer is **(A)** $90$.

wrong_choices.E: $360$ is the area of the pan in square inches, $20 \times 18$. Each piece covers $4$ square inches, so the number of pieces is much smaller.
wrong_choices.C: $180$ comes from dividing the area $360$ by $2$. A piece is $2$ inches by $2$ inches, so its area is $4$, and you must divide by $4$.

verification.verifier_notes: Passed adversarial verifier on first review.
